8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

title arborparser Model

class AutoPruneStrategy {
    addNodeAndUpdateBranch(node : ChainNode, currentBranch : List<TreeNode>) : void
    addNodeToTree(node : ChainNode, currentBranch : List<TreeNode>, currentNodeRef : node) : void
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    createTreeNode(chainnode : ChainNode) : TreeNode
    isAllNotImmNodesSiblings(queue : Deque) : void
}
class BaseNode {
    content : String
    levelSeq : List<int>
    levelText : String
    title : String
    concatNode(node : BaseNode) : void
}
class ChainNode {
    patternPriority : int
}
class ChainParser {
    patterns : List<LevelPattern>
    createChainNode(levelSeq : List<int>, title : String, content : String, levelText : String, patternPriority : int) : ChainNode
    detectLevel(line : String) : ChainNode
    parseToChain(text : String) : List<ChainNode>
}
class LevelPattern {
    description : String
    failOnConvert : boolean
    fixedLevelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>
    maxLevel : int
    minLevel : int
    numberType : NumberType
    regexText : String
    separator : String
    helper : ParserHelper
    convertMatchedText(matchedText : String) : List<EIntegerObject>
    getRegex() : Pattern
}
class ParserHelper {
    convertNumber(numberType : NumberType, text : String) : EIntegerObject
    getNumberPattern(numberType : NumberType) : String
}
class PatternBuilder {
    maxLevel : int
    minLevel : int
    numberType : NumberType
    prefixRegex : String
    separator : String
    suffixRegex : String
    build() : LevelPattern
    copySelf() : PatternBuilder
    modify(newPrefixRegex : String, newMinLevel : int) : PatternBuilder
    validate() : void
}
class StrictStrategy {
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    createTreeNode(chainnode : ChainNode) : TreeNode
    isChild(parentSeq : List<EIntegerObject>, childSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : boolean
}
class TreeBuilder {
    strategy : TreeBuildingStrategy
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
}
abstract class TreeBuildingStrategy {
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    getLastLevel(levelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : int
    getPrefix(levelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : List<EIntegerObject>
    isImmNext(frontSeq : List<EIntegerObject>, backSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : boolean
    isRoot(node : BaseNode) : boolean
}
class TreeExporter {
    escapeJson(s : String) : String
    exportChain(chain : List<ChainNode>) : String
    exportToJson(tree : TreeNode) : String
    exportToJsonFile(tree : TreeNode, filePath : Path) : void
    exportTree(tree : TreeNode) : String
    exportTreeInternal(node : TreeNode, prefix : String, isLast : boolean, isRoot : boolean) : String
    nodeToDict(node : TreeNode) : EMap
    toJson(obj : EJavaObject, indent : int) : String
}
class TreeNode {
    children : List<TreeNode>
    parent : TreeNode
    addChild(child : TreeNode) : void
    getFullContent() : String
    mergeAllChildren() : void
}
enum NumberType {
    ARABIC
    ROMAN
    CHINESE
    LETTER
    CIRCLED
}

AutoPruneStrategy --|> TreeBuildingStrategy
ChainNode --|> BaseNode
ChainParser *-- "*" LevelPattern : patterns
LevelPattern --> ParserHelper : helper
StrictStrategy --|> TreeBuildingStrategy
TreeBuilder --> TreeBuildingStrategy : strategy
TreeNode --|> BaseNode
TreeNode *-- "*" TreeNode : children  'opposite: parent
TreeNode --> TreeNode : parent  'opposite: children
@enduml

abstract class TreeBuildingStrategy {
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    getLastLevel(levelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : int
    getPrefix(levelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : List<EIntegerObject>
    isImmNext(frontSeq : List<EIntegerObject>, backSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : boolean
    isRoot(node : BaseNode) : boolean
}
class TreeExporter {
    escapeJson(s : String) : String
    exportChain(chain : List<ChainNode>) : String
    exportToJson(tree : TreeNode) : String
    exportToJsonFile(tree : TreeNode, filePath : Path) : void
    exportTree(tree : TreeNode) : String
    exportTreeInternal(node : TreeNode, prefix : String, isLast : boolean, isRoot : boolean) : String
    nodeToDict(node : TreeNode) : EMap
    toJson(obj : EJavaObject, indent : int) : String
}
class TreeNode {
    children : List<TreeNode>
    parent : TreeNode
    addChild(child : TreeNode) : void
    getFullContent() : String
    mergeAllChildren() : void
}
enum NumberType {
    ARABIC
    ROMAN
    CHINESE
    LETTER
    CIRCLED
}

AutoPruneStrategy --|> TreeBuildingStrategy
ChainNode --|> BaseNode
ChainParser *-- "*" LevelPattern : patterns
LevelPattern --> ParserHelper : helper
StrictStrategy --|> TreeBuildingStrategy
TreeBuilder --> TreeBuildingStrategy : strategy
TreeNode --|> BaseNode
TreeNode *-- "*" TreeNode : children  'opposite: parent
TreeNode --> TreeNode : parent  'opposite: children
@enduml
```

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
TreeNode::mergeAllChildren
Summary:
Merges all descendant content into this node and removes child structure by collecting the children’s text in traversal order.
Algorithm:
1. For each child in order, obtain its full content.
2. Append each child's content to this node's content without inserting extra separators.
3. Remove or clear the children list after merging, while keeping this node as the content container.
4. Ensure parent links of removed children are no longer active if the implementation detaches them.
Related Features:
- Subtree content flattening
- Traversal-order merge
Related Classes: TreeNode
Input:
- None.
Output:
- None.
Pre-condition:
- The node may have zero or more children.
Post-condition:
- The node content includes all descendant content in order.
- The node's child collection is empty or detached according to the implementation.

TreeNode::getFullContent
Summary:
Returns the full section content by concatenating this node's content with all descendant contents in traversal order.
Algorithm:
1. Start with this.content.
2. Traverse children in their stored order.
3. Append each child's full content recursively.
4. Return the concatenated result without extra separators.
Related Features:
- Descendant content aggregation
- Traversal-order concatenation
Related Classes: TreeNode
Input:
- None.
Output:
- A string containing the full content of the subtree.
Pre-condition:
- The tree structure is well-formed.
Post-condition:
- No tree links are modified.

TreeNode::addChild
Summary:
Adds a child node to this node and updates the bidirectional parent-child relationship.
Algorithm:
1. Append child to this.children.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
TreeNode::mergeAllChildren
Summary:
Merges all descendant content into this node and removes child structure by collecting the children’s text in traversal order.
Algorithm:
1. For each child in order, obtain its full content.
2. Append each child's content to this node's content without inserting extra separators.
3. Remove or clear the children list after merging, while keeping this node as the content container.
4. Ensure parent links of removed children are no longer active if the implementation detaches them.
Related Features:
- Subtree content flattening
- Traversal-order merge
Related Classes: TreeNode
Input:
- None.
Output:
- None.
Pre-condition:
- The node may have zero or more children.
Post-condition:
- The node content includes all descendant content in order.
- The node's child collection is empty or detached according to the implementation.

TreeNode::getFullContent
Summary:
Returns the full section content by concatenating this node's content with all descendant contents in traversal order.
Algorithm:
1. Start with this.content.
2. Traverse children in their stored order.
3. Append each child's full content recursively.
4. Return the concatenated result without extra separators.
Related Features:
- Descendant content aggregation
- Traversal-order concatenation
Related Classes: TreeNode
Input:
- None.
Output:
- A string containing the full content of the subtree.
Pre-condition:
- The tree structure is well-formed.
Post-condition:
- No tree links are modified.

TreeNode::addChild
Summary:
Adds a child node to this node and updates the bidirectional parent-child relationship.
Algorithm:
1. Append child to this.children.
2. Set child.parent to this.
3. Preserve existing order by appending at the end.
Related Features:
- Parent-child link maintenance
- Ordered child insertion
Related Classes: TreeNode
Input:
- child: TreeNode to be added as a child.
Output:
- None.
Pre-condition:
- child is non-null.
- child is not already attached in a conflicting way.
Post-condition:
- This node contains child in its children list.
- child.parent points back to this node.

# Operation Specifications
TreeBuildingStrategy::isRoot
Summary:
Determines whether a node is the synthetic or logical root node.
Algorithm:
1. Check whether the node's level sequence is empty.
2. If a title-based root convention is used, also accept the synthetic title "ROOT" with empty sequence.
3. Return the result.
Related Features:
- Root detection
Related Classes: BaseNode
Input:
- node: a BaseNode to test.
Output:
- Boolean indicating whether the node is the root.
Pre-condition:
- node is non-null.
Post-condition:
- The node is not modified.

TreeBuildingStrategy::getPrefix
Summary:
Returns the parent prefix of a level sequence by removing its last segment.
Algorithm:
1. If the sequence is empty, return an empty sequence.
2. Otherwise, return a copy of the sequence excluding the last element.
Related Features:
- Prefix derivation
- Parent-sequence computation
Related Classes: None
Input:
- levelSeq: a list of integer level components.
Output:
- The prefix sequence.
Pre-condition:
- levelSeq is non-null.
Post-condition:
- Returned prefix is independent of the input list.

TreeBuildingStrategy::getLastLevel
Summary:
Returns the last integer in a level sequence, representing the immediate local ordinal at the deepest level.
Algorithm:
1. Ensure the sequence is non-empty.
2. Return the last element of the sequence.
Related Features:
- Level-sequence inspection
Related Classes: None
Input:
- levelSeq: a list of integer level components.
Output:
- The last level value.
Pre-condition:
- levelSeq is non-null and non-empty.
Post-condition:
- The input sequence is not modified.

# Operation Specifications
TreeBuildingStrategy::isRoot
Summary:
Determines whether a node is the synthetic or logical root node.
Algorithm:
1. Check whether the node's level sequence is empty.
2. If a title-based root convention is used, also accept the synthetic title "ROOT" with empty sequence.
3. Return the result.
Related Features:
- Root detection
Related Classes: BaseNode
Input:
- node: a BaseNode to test.
Output:
- Boolean indicating whether the node is the root.
Pre-condition:
- node is non-null.
Post-condition:
- The node is not modified.

TreeBuildingStrategy::getPrefix
Summary:
Returns the parent prefix of a level sequence by removing its last segment.
Algorithm:
1. If the sequence is empty, return an empty sequence.
2. Otherwise, return a copy of the sequence excluding the last element.
Related Features:
- Prefix derivation
- Parent-sequence computation
Related Classes: None
Input:
- levelSeq: a list of integer level components.
Output:
- The prefix sequence.
Pre-condition:
- levelSeq is non-null.
Post-condition:
- Returned prefix is independent of the input list.

TreeBuildingStrategy::getLastLevel
Summary:
Returns the last integer in a level sequence, representing the immediate local ordinal at the deepest level.
Algorithm:
1. Ensure the sequence is non-empty.
2. Return the last element of the sequence.
Related Features:
- Level-sequence inspection
Related Classes: None
Input:
- levelSeq: a list of integer level components.
Output:
- The last level value.
Pre-condition:
- levelSeq is non-null and non-empty.
Post-condition:
- The input sequence is not modified.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

- The receiver content includes the appended content of node.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

# Operation Specifications
AutoPruneStrategy::addNodeToTree
Summary:
Attaches one chain node to the tree under the nearest suitable ancestor in the current branch.
Algorithm:
1. Convert the ChainNode into a TreeNode.
2. Search currentBranch from tail to head for the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is a prefix of node.levelSeq.
3. Attach the created TreeNode as a child of that ancestor.
4. Update currentNodeRef to the newly attached TreeNode.
5. Remove any branch nodes that are no longer on the path to the new node and append the new node to currentBranch.
Related Features:
- TreeNode creation from ChainNode
- Prefix-based ancestry selection
- Parent-child link maintenance
- Branch update for auto-prune strategy
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy
Input:
- node: the ChainNode to be attached.
- currentBranch: mutable branch path used to locate the attachment point.
- currentNodeRef: reference to the current active TreeNode node; updated to the inserted node.
Output:
- None.
Pre-condition:
- node is non-null and has a level sequence.
- currentBranch contains at least the root.
Post-condition:
- The new node is inserted into the tree at the nearest valid ancestor.
- currentNodeRef refers to the inserted tree node.
- currentBranch reflects the updated path to the inserted node.

AutoPruneStrategy::isAllNotImmNodesSiblings
Summary:
Checks whether all nodes currently in the pending queue form an immediate sibling sequence.
Algorithm:
1. If the queue contains fewer than 2 nodes, treat it as not sufficient for sibling-sequence confirmation.
2. Examine the nodes in arrival order.
3. For every adjacent pair, test whether they are immediate siblings:
   - Their level sequences share the same prefix.
   - Their last levels differ by exactly 1.
4. Return true only if all adjacent pairs satisfy the sibling condition.
Related Features:
- Pending queue analysis
- Immediate sibling relation detection
Related Classes: TreeBuildingStrategy
Input:
- queue: a deque of pending nodes.
Output:
- Boolean indicating whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence.
Pre-condition:
- queue is non-null.
Post-condition:
- The queue content is not modified.

AutoPruneStrategy::addNodeAndUpdateBranch
Summary:
Adds one chain node into the current auto-prune construction branch and updates the latest valid branch from root to the current node.
Algorithm:
1. Determine whether the incoming node is an immediate valid next node of the current branch tail using the level-sequence relation.
2. If it is immediate:
   - Find the nearest ancestor in currentBranch whose level sequence is a prefix of the new node.
   - Attach the node to that ancestor via addNodeToTree.
   - Truncate currentBranch to that ancestor and append the new tree node.
3. If it is not immediate:
   - Place the node into the pending queue maintained by the auto-prune strategy.
   - If the pending queue size reaches 3, test whether all pending nodes are immediate siblings.
   - If yes, attach them in arrival order.
   - Otherwise, merge the oldest pending node into the content of the current node.
4. Preserve parent-child links and update the reference to the current node.
Related Features:
- Uses the auto-prune pending queue behavior
- Uses currentBranch as the latest valid path
- Uses immediate-next and prefix relations from TreeBuildingStrategy
- Uses TreeNode.parent and TreeNode.children consistency
- Uses BaseNode.content concatenation when merging
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy
Input:
- node: the next ChainNode to process.
- currentBranch: mutable list of TreeNode representing the current valid branch from root to the latest attached node.
Output:
- None.
Pre-condition:
- currentBranch is non-null and contains at least the root node.
- node is non-null.
- The node has a valid level sequence or is intended for pending/merge handling.
Post-condition:
- If node is immediate, it is attached to the appropriate ancestor and currentBranch is updated.
- If node is non-immediate, it is stored in the pending queue or merged according to the auto-prune rules.
- Tree parent-child relationships remain consistent after any attachment.

AutoPruneStrategy::createTreeNode
Summary:
Creates a TreeNode instance from a ChainNode, copying structural and textual fields.
Algorithm:
1. Instantiate a new TreeNode.
2. Copy title, levelSeq, levelText, and content from the ChainNode into the new TreeNode.
3. Initialize children as empty and parent as null.
4. Return the created node.
Related Features:
- Node materialization for tree building
- Field copying from chain to tree node
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode
Input:
- chainnode: the ChainNode to convert.
Output:
- A new TreeNode carrying the same semantic fields as the input ChainNode.
Pre-condition:
- chainnode is non-null.
Post-condition:
- Returned node is independent from the input chain node except for copied values.
- The returned node has no parent and no children.

AutoPruneStrategy::buildTree
Summary:
Builds a document tree using the auto-prune strategy, recovering from irregular level jumps by deferring or merging nodes when necessary.
Algorithm:
1. Create a synthetic root node titled "ROOT" with empty level sequence.
2. Initialize currentBranch with the root and clear the pending queue.
3. Iterate through the chain in order:
   - For each node, decide whether it is immediate-next relative to the current branch tail.
   - If immediate, attach it using addNodeAndUpdateBranch.
   - Otherwise, enqueue it as pending and apply the pending-queue rules:
     a. If queue size is 3, check whether the three pending nodes are siblings.
     b. If siblings, attach them in order.
     c. Otherwise, merge the oldest pending node into the current node's content.
4. After all nodes are processed, merge any remaining pending nodes into the current node's content.
5. Return the root.
Related Features:
- Root synthesis for empty/unmatched documents
- Pending queue management
- Irregular jump recovery
- Auto-prune sibling grouping
- Content merging in traversal order
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy
Input:
- chain: ordered list of ChainNode objects parsed from the source text.
Output:
- root TreeNode representing the reconstructed document outline tree.
Pre-condition:
- chain is non-null; it may be empty.
- Each ChainNode has a title, content, and level sequence or is otherwise mergeable.
Post-condition:
- A tree rooted at "ROOT" is returned.
- All input nodes are either attached into the tree or merged into section content.
- Tree ordering is deterministic and consistent with input order and auto-prune rules.

 */

class_1::operation_2

 */

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
AutoPruneStrategy::addNodeToTree
Summary:
Attaches one chain node to the tree under the nearest suitable ancestor in the current branch.
Algorithm:
1. Convert the ChainNode into a TreeNode.
2. Search currentBranch from tail to head for the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is a prefix of node.levelSeq.
3. Attach the created TreeNode as a child of that ancestor.
4. Update currentNodeRef to the newly attached TreeNode.
5. Remove any branch nodes that are no longer on the path to the new node and append the new node to currentBranch.
Related Features:
- TreeNode creation from ChainNode
- Prefix-based ancestry selection
- Parent-child link maintenance
- Branch update for auto-prune strategy
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy
Input:
- node: the ChainNode to be attached.
- currentBranch: mutable branch path used to locate the attachment point.
- currentNodeRef: reference to the current active TreeNode node; updated to the inserted node.
Output:
- None.
Pre-condition:
- node is non-null and has a level sequence.
- currentBranch contains at least the root.
Post-condition:
- The new node is inserted into the tree at the nearest valid ancestor.
- currentNodeRef refers to the inserted tree node.
- currentBranch reflects the updated path to the inserted node.

AutoPruneStrategy::isAllNotImmNodesSiblings
Summary:
Checks whether all nodes currently in the pending queue form an immediate sibling sequence.
Algorithm:
1. If the queue contains fewer than 2 nodes, treat it as not sufficient for sibling-sequence confirmation.
2. Examine the nodes in arrival order.
3. For every adjacent pair, test whether they are immediate siblings:
   - Their level sequences share the same prefix.
   - Their last levels differ by exactly 1.
4. Return true only if all adjacent pairs satisfy the sibling condition.
Related Features:
- Pending queue analysis
- Immediate sibling relation detection
Related Classes: TreeBuildingStrategy
Input:
- queue: a deque of pending nodes.
Output:
- Boolean indicating whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence.
Pre-condition:
- queue is non-null.
Post-condition:
- The queue content is not modified.

AutoPruneStrategy::addNodeAndUpdateBranch
Summary:
Adds one chain node into the current auto-prune construction branch and updates the latest valid branch from root to the current node.
Algorithm:
1. Determine whether the incoming node is an immediate valid next node of the current branch tail using the level-sequence relation.
2. If it is immediate:
   - Find the nearest ancestor in currentBranch whose level sequence is a prefix of the new node.
   - Attach the node to that ancestor via addNodeToTree.
   - Truncate currentBranch to that ancestor and append the new tree node.
3. If it is not immediate:
   - Place the node into the pending queue maintained by the auto-prune strategy.
   - If the pending queue size reaches 3, test whether all pending nodes are immediate siblings.
   - If yes, attach them in arrival order.
   - Otherwise, merge the oldest pending node into the content of the current node.
4. Preserve parent-child links and update the reference to the current node.
Related Features:
- Uses the auto-prune pending queue behavior
- Uses currentBranch as the latest valid path
- Uses immediate-next and prefix relations from TreeBuildingStrategy
- Uses TreeNode.parent and TreeNode.children consistency
- Uses BaseNode.content concatenation when merging
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy
Input:
- node: the next ChainNode to process.
- currentBranch: mutable list of TreeNode representing the current valid branch from root to the latest attached node.
Output:
- None.
Pre-condition:
- currentBranch is non-null and contains at least the root node.
- node is non-null.
- The node has a valid level sequence or is intended for pending/merge handling.
Post-condition:
- If node is immediate, it is attached to the appropriate ancestor and currentBranch is updated.
- If node is non-immediate, it is stored in the pending queue or merged according to the auto-prune rules.
- Tree parent-child relationships remain consistent after any attachment.

AutoPruneStrategy::createTreeNode
Summary:
Creates a TreeNode instance from a ChainNode, copying structural and textual fields.
Algorithm:
1. Instantiate a new TreeNode.
2. Copy title, levelSeq, levelText, and content from the ChainNode into the new TreeNode.
3. Initialize children as empty and parent as null.
4. Return the created node.
Related Features:
- Node materialization for tree building
- Field copying from chain to tree node
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode
Input:
- chainnode: the ChainNode to convert.
Output:
- A new TreeNode carrying the same semantic fields as the input ChainNode.
Pre-condition:
- chainnode is non-null.
Post-condition:
- Returned node is independent from the input chain node except for copied values.
- The returned node has no parent and no children.

AutoPruneStrategy::buildTree
Summary:
Builds a document tree using the auto-prune strategy, recovering from irregular level jumps by deferring or merging nodes when necessary.
Algorithm:
1. Create a synthetic root node titled "ROOT" with empty level sequence.
2. Initialize currentBranch with the root and clear the pending queue.
3. Iterate through the chain in order:
   - For each node, decide whether it is immediate-next relative to the current branch tail.
   - If immediate, attach it using addNodeAndUpdateBranch.
   - Otherwise, enqueue it as pending and apply the pending-queue rules:
     a. If queue size is 3, check whether the three pending nodes are siblings.
     b. If siblings, attach them in order.
     c. Otherwise, merge the oldest pending node into the current node's content.
4. After all nodes are processed, merge any remaining pending nodes into the current node's content.
5. Return the root.
Related Features:
- Root synthesis for empty/unmatched documents
- Pending queue management
- Irregular jump recovery
- Auto-prune sibling grouping
- Content merging in traversal order
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy
Input:
- chain: ordered list of ChainNode objects parsed from the source text.
Output:
- root TreeNode representing the reconstructed document outline tree.
Pre-condition:
- chain is non-null; it may be empty.
- Each ChainNode has a title, content, and level sequence or is otherwise mergeable.
Post-condition:
- A tree rooted at "ROOT" is returned.
- All input nodes are either attached into the tree or merged into section content.
- Tree ordering is deterministic and consistent with input order and auto-prune rules.

    addNodeAndUpdateBranch(node : ChainNode, currentBranch : List<TreeNode>) : void
    addNodeToTree(node : ChainNode, currentBranch : List<TreeNode>, currentNodeRef : node) : void
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    createTreeNode(chainnode : ChainNode) : TreeNode
    isAllNotImmNodesSiblings(queue : Deque) : void
}

    content : String
    levelSeq : List<int>
    levelText : String
    title : String
    concatNode(node : BaseNode) : void
}

    patternPriority : int
}

    patterns : List<LevelPattern>

    parseToChain(text : String) : List<ChainNode>
}

}

    getNumberPattern(numberType : NumberType) : String
}

    maxLevel : int
    minLevel : int
    numberType : NumberType
    prefixRegex : String
    separator : String
    suffixRegex : String

    validate() : void
}
class StrictStrategy {
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    createTreeNode(chainnode : ChainNode) : TreeNode

}

    strategy : TreeBuildingStrategy
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
}
abstract class TreeBuildingStrategy {

}

}

    mergeAllChildren() : void
}

    LETTER
    CIRCLED
}

      - Merge any pending nodes that appear before it into the current node content in arrival order.
      - Attach the node at the nearest suitable ancestor.
      - Update currentBranch to the new valid branch.
   b. Otherwise:
      - Push node into the pending queue.
      - If pending size reaches 3:
        i. Check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence.
        ii. If yes, attach them to the tree in order.
        iii. If no, merge the oldest pending node into current node content.
4. After all nodes are processed, merge any remaining pending nodes into the current node content in arrival order.
5. Return the root tree.
Related Features:
- Synthetic root creation
- Auto-prune pending queue handling
- Immediate sibling-sequence recovery
- Content merging in traversal order
- Branch update after attachment
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy
Input:
- chain: ordered list of ChainNode objects parsed from text.
Output:
- A TreeNode representing the root of the constructed outline tree.
Pre-condition:

- Each ChainNode should have a parsed levelSeq or be representable as content-only input.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
TreeNode::mergeAllChildren
Summary:
Merge all descendant content into this node’s content and remove or neutralize child nodes according to the tree’s pruning semantics, while preserving content order.
Algorithm:
1. Traverse children in order and collect each child’s full content.
2. Concatenate the collected content into this.content without separators.
3. Recursively process descendants if pruning semantics require deeper merging.
4. If the strategy expects structural pruning, clear children after merging and keep parent references consistent.
Related Features:
- Descendant content merge
- Structural pruning
- Traversal-order content preservation
Related Classes: TreeNode
Input:
- None.
Output:
- None.
Pre-condition:
- The node is part of a valid tree.
Post-condition:
- The node content includes merged descendant content, and the child structure is updated consistently with the merge policy.

TreeNode::getFullContent
Summary:
Collect the full textual content of this node, including its own content and the content of descendants, in traversal order without extra separators.
Algorithm:
1. Start with this.content.
2. Traverse children in stored order.
3. Append each descendant's full content to the result.
4. Return the concatenated string.
Related Features:
- Recursive content collection
- Traversal-order concatenation
- No-extra-separator merge semantics
Related Classes: TreeNode
Input:
- None.
Output:
- A string containing the node’s complete content aggregation.
Pre-condition:
- The tree structure rooted at this node is acyclic.
Post-condition:
- No tree state is modified.

TreeNode::addChild
Summary:
Attach a child node to this node while maintaining bidirectional parent-child consistency.
Algorithm:
1. Append child to this.children.
2. Set child.parent to this.
3. Preserve existing child order by appending to the end.
Related Features:
- Tree structure mutation
- Parent-child link consistency
- Ordered children
Related Classes: TreeNode
Input:
- child: TreeNode to attach.
Output:
- None.
Pre-condition:
- child is not null.
- child is not already attached elsewhere, or reattachment semantics are explicitly allowed by the caller.
Post-condition:
- child is listed in this.children and its parent points back to this node.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
TreeBuildingStrategy::isRoot
Summary:
Determine whether a node is the synthetic or semantic root of the outline tree.
Algorithm:
1. Check whether node.levelSeq is empty.
2. Optionally confirm that the title equals "ROOT" for synthetic root nodes.
3. Return true if the node represents root semantics.
Related Features:
- Root identification
- Synthetic root support
Related Classes: BaseNode
Input:
- node: a BaseNode candidate.
Output:
- Boolean indicating whether the node is root.
Pre-condition:
- node is not null.
Post-condition:
- No state is modified.

TreeBuildingStrategy::getPrefix
Summary:
Return the prefix of a level sequence, excluding its last component, for use in ancestor and sibling comparisons.
Algorithm:
1. If levelSeq is empty, return an empty list.
2. Otherwise, return a new list containing all elements except the last one.
Related Features:
- Prefix extraction
- Ancestor comparison support
Related Classes: None
Input:
- levelSeq: list of integer level components.
Output:
- Prefix list of the input sequence.
Pre-condition:
- levelSeq is not null.
Post-condition:
- The returned list is independent from the original sequence.

TreeBuildingStrategy::getLastLevel
Summary:
Get the last integer level value from a level sequence.
Algorithm:
1. If levelSeq is empty, return a sentinel value such as 0 or -1 according to system convention.
2. Otherwise, return the last element of levelSeq.
Related Features:
- Sequence inspection
- Level comparison support
Related Classes: None
Input:
- levelSeq: list of integer level components.
Output:
- The last level component, or a sentinel for empty input.
Pre-condition:
- levelSeq is not null.
Post-condition:
- No state is modified.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
TreeBuildingStrategy::isRoot
Summary:
Determine whether a node is the synthetic or semantic root of the outline tree.
Algorithm:
1. Check whether node.levelSeq is empty.
2. Optionally confirm that the title equals "ROOT" for synthetic root nodes.
3. Return true if the node represents root semantics.
Related Features:
- Root identification
- Synthetic root support
Related Classes: BaseNode
Input:
- node: a BaseNode candidate.
Output:
- Boolean indicating whether the node is root.
Pre-condition:
- node is not null.
Post-condition:
- No state is modified.

TreeBuildingStrategy::getPrefix
Summary:
Return the prefix of a level sequence, excluding its last component, for use in ancestor and sibling comparisons.
Algorithm:
1. If levelSeq is empty, return an empty list.
2. Otherwise, return a new list containing all elements except the last one.
Related Features:
- Prefix extraction
- Ancestor comparison support
Related Classes: None
Input:
- levelSeq: list of integer level components.
Output:
- Prefix list of the input sequence.
Pre-condition:
- levelSeq is not null.
Post-condition:
- The returned list is independent from the original sequence.

TreeBuildingStrategy::getLastLevel
Summary:
Get the last integer level value from a level sequence.
Algorithm:
1. If levelSeq is empty, return a sentinel value such as 0 or -1 according to system convention.
2. Otherwise, return the last element of levelSeq.
Related Features:
- Sequence inspection
- Level comparison support
Related Classes: None
Input:
- levelSeq: list of integer level components.
Output:
- The last level component, or a sentinel for empty input.
Pre-condition:
- levelSeq is not null.
Post-condition:
- No state is modified.

# Operation Specifications
BaseNode::concatNode
Summary:
Concatenate another node's content into this node using traversal-order concatenation without inserting extra separators, and update textual fields as needed to keep the node semantically consistent.
Algorithm:
1. If node.content is non-empty, append it directly to this.content.
2. If this.content is empty, replace it with node.content.
3. Optionally merge title/level text only if the implementation treats the merged node as content-bearing text source; otherwise preserve the current structural fields.
4. Do not insert spaces, line breaks, or other separators between concatenated fragments.
Related Features:
- Content accumulation
- Traversal-order merging
- No-extra-separator concatenation
Related Classes: BaseNode
Input:
- node: another BaseNode whose content is to be merged into this node.
Output:
- None.
Pre-condition:
- node is not null.
Post-condition:
- this.content contains the concatenation of the previous content and node.content in order.

# Operation Specifications
BaseNode::concatNode
Summary:
Concatenate another node's content into this node using traversal-order concatenation without inserting extra separators, and update textual fields as needed to keep the node semantically consistent.
Algorithm:
1. If node.content is non-empty, append it directly to this.content.
2. If this.content is empty, replace it with node.content.
3. Optionally merge title/level text only if the implementation treats the merged node as content-bearing text source; otherwise preserve the current structural fields.
4. Do not insert spaces, line breaks, or other separators between concatenated fragments.
Related Features:
- Content accumulation
- Traversal-order merging
- No-extra-separator concatenation
Related Classes: BaseNode
Input:
- node: another BaseNode whose content is to be merged into this node.
Output:
- None.
Pre-condition:
- node is not null.
Post-condition:
- this.content contains the concatenation of the previous content and node.content in order.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

- Tree construction entry point

- chain: ordered list of ChainNode objects.
Output:
- Root TreeNode of the built outline tree.

- strategy is not null.
Post-condition:
- The tree result follows the selected strategy’s semantics.

# Operation Specifications
AutoPruneStrategy::addNodeToTree
Summary:
Attach a chain node to the tree under the appropriate ancestor in the current branch, and update the current node reference used by auto-prune logic.
Algorithm:
1. Create a TreeNode from node.
2. Find the nearest ancestor in currentBranch whose level sequence is the prefix of node.levelSeq.
3. Add the created TreeNode as a child of that ancestor.
4. Update currentNodeRef to point to the newly attached TreeNode.
5. Adjust currentBranch so that it ends at currentNodeRef.
Related Features:
- Node-to-tree conversion
- Parent-child link maintenance
- Branch tail update
- Prefix-based attachment
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode
Input:
- node: a ChainNode to attach.
- currentBranch: current branch path from root to the latest node.
- currentNodeRef: reference to the current node state used by the strategy.
Output:
- None.
Pre-condition:
- node is valid and ready to be attached.
- currentBranch contains at least the root node.
Post-condition:
- A new TreeNode corresponding to node exists in the tree.
- currentNodeRef points to the inserted node.
- Parent-child consistency is preserved.

AutoPruneStrategy::isAllNotImmNodesSiblings
Summary:
Determine whether all nodes currently stored in the pending queue form an immediate sibling sequence, meaning they share the same parent prefix and advance by one level-step among adjacent nodes.
Algorithm:
1. If queue has fewer than 3 nodes, return false.
2. Inspect the nodes in arrival order.
3. Check that every adjacent pair is an immediate-next sibling relation:
   a. Their prefixes are equal.
   b. Their last level values advance by exactly one.
4. Return true only if all nodes satisfy the sibling-sequence relation.
Related Features:
- Pending queue recovery check
- Immediate sibling-sequence validation
Related Classes: None
Input:
- queue: deque of pending chain nodes.
Output:
- Boolean result indicating whether the queue elements form an immediate sibling sequence.
Pre-condition:
- queue is not null.
Post-condition:
- No structural state is changed.

AutoPruneStrategy::addNodeAndUpdateBranch
Summary:
Update the current valid branch in auto-prune tree construction when a new chain node is processed. If the new node is an immediate valid next node, extend the branch by attaching it at the nearest suitable ancestor. Otherwise, keep the branch stable and allow the node to be handled through the pending-node mechanism used by auto-prune.
Algorithm:
1. Inspect node.levelSeq and compare it with the level sequence of nodes in currentBranch.
2. If node is an immediate valid next node relative to the current branch:
   a. Find the nearest ancestor in currentBranch whose level sequence is the prefix of node.levelSeq.
   b. Attach the created TreeNode for node under that ancestor.
   c. Replace the branch tail with the newly attached node and prune any deeper invalid branch state.
3. If node is not an immediate valid next node:
   a. Do not attach it immediately.
   b. Preserve currentBranch and let the caller manage pending queue handling.
4. Ensure branch consistency from root to the latest attached node.
Related Features:
- Auto-prune branch maintenance during tree construction
- Immediate-next-node detection and recovery from irregular level jumps
- Parent-child consistency after node attachment
- Pending-node deferral strategy
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy
Input:
- node: a ChainNode to be processed.
- currentBranch: ordered list of TreeNode objects representing the current valid branch from root to the latest attached node.
Output:
- None.
Pre-condition:
- currentBranch is initialized and contains a valid branch path.
- node is not null and has a valid levelSeq if it is intended to be attached.
Post-condition:
- If node is immediately attachable, the tree and currentBranch reflect the new branch endpoint.
- If node is not attachable, currentBranch remains consistent and node is left for pending handling.

AutoPruneStrategy::createTreeNode
Summary:
Create a TreeNode from a ChainNode by copying structural and textual attributes.
Algorithm:
1. Allocate a new TreeNode.
2. Copy title, levelSeq, levelText, content, and any other applicable BaseNode fields from chainnode.
3. Initialize children to empty and parent to null.
4. Return the new TreeNode.
Related Features:
- Node conversion from chain to tree
- Field copying of outline data
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode
Input:
- chainnode: the source ChainNode.
Output:
- A newly created TreeNode mirroring chainnode data.
Pre-condition:
- chainnode is not null.
Post-condition:
- The returned TreeNode contains the same semantic node data as chainnode and is not linked into any tree yet.

AutoPruneStrategy::buildTree
Summary:
Build a document outline tree from a list of chain nodes using the auto-prune strategy. The strategy maintains a branch, defers irregular nodes into a pending queue, merges pending nodes into content when appropriate, and recovers from invalid jumps using sibling-sequence checks.
Algorithm:
1. Create a synthetic root TreeNode titled "ROOT" with empty level sequence.
2. Initialize currentBranch with the root and initialize an empty pending queue.
3. For each node in chain:
   a. If node is an immediate valid next node:
      - Merge any pending nodes that appear before it into the current node content in arrival order.
      - Attach the node at the nearest suitable ancestor.
      - Update currentBranch to the new valid branch.
   b. Otherwise:
      - Push node into the pending queue.
      - If pending size reaches 3:
        i. Check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence.
        ii. If yes, attach them to the tree in order.
        iii. If no, merge the oldest pending node into current node content.
4. After all nodes are processed, merge any remaining pending nodes into the current node content in arrival order.
5. Return the root tree.
Related Features:
- Synthetic root creation
- Auto-prune pending queue handling
- Immediate sibling-sequence recovery
- Content merging in traversal order
- Branch update after attachment
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy
Input:
- chain: ordered list of ChainNode objects parsed from text.
Output:
- A TreeNode representing the root of the constructed outline tree.
Pre-condition:
- chain may be empty, but must be iterable.
- Each ChainNode should have a parsed levelSeq or be representable as content-only input.
Post-condition:
- The result is a tree rooted at a synthetic node titled "ROOT".
- All input nodes are either attached into the tree or merged into content according to auto-prune rules.
