# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
ChainParser::parseToChain
Summary:
Parse a full text document into an ordered chain of ChainNode objects, preserving both heading lines and ordinary content lines.
Algorithm:
1. Split text into lines using document line boundaries.
2. For each line:
   a. Call detectLevel(line).
   b. Append the returned ChainNode to the output chain.
3. Preserve document order.
4. Return the chain.
Related Features:
- Document line parsing
- Ordered chain generation
- Content preservation
Related Classes: ChainNode
Input:
- text: raw structured text, possibly empty.
Output:
- Ordered list of ChainNode objects.
Pre-condition:
- text is not null.
Post-condition:
- The returned chain contains one parsed node per source line, including content-only lines when headings are not recognized.

ChainParser::detectLevel
Summary:
Detect whether a line is a valid heading by trying configured level patterns in order, and return the first successful parse as a ChainNode. If no valid pattern matches, treat the line as content rather than a heading.
Algorithm:
1. Iterate over patterns in ascending order of priority.
2. For each pattern:
   a. Match the line against pattern regex.
   b. If matched, convert the matched numbering text into a level sequence.
   c. If conversion succeeds and produces a valid level sequence, extract title and content.
   d. Return a created ChainNode with the corresponding patternPriority.
3. If no pattern matches or all conversions fail:
   a. Return a non-heading ChainNode or an equivalent content node with empty/invalid level information, depending on parser conventions.
Related Features:
- Pattern-driven heading recognition
- First-valid-pattern wins
- Number conversion validation
- Content fallback for unmatched lines
Related Classes: ChainNode, LevelPattern, ParserHelper
Input:
- line: one line of structured text.
Output:
- A ChainNode describing the detected heading or content fallback.
Pre-condition:
- patterns is initialized.
- line is not null; empty lines are allowed as content.
Post-condition:
- The returned node reflects the first valid matching pattern, or a content-like node if no heading is recognized.

ChainParser::createChainNode
Summary:
Create a ChainNode representing one parsed heading or content-bearing line using the provided structural attributes.
Algorithm:
1. Allocate a new ChainNode.
2. Set levelSeq, title, content, levelText, and patternPriority from the arguments.
3. Return the created node.
Related Features:
- Parsed-node materialization
- Pattern-priority preservation
Related Classes: ChainNode
Input:
- levelSeq: integer sequence describing the heading level.
- title: heading title text.
- content: content text associated with the line.
- levelText: the matched level indicator text.
- patternPriority: priority of the matched pattern.
Output:
- A new ChainNode instance.
Pre-condition:
- Inputs are consistent with a recognized line or a content node.
Post-condition:
- Returned node stores the supplied semantic information for later tree construction.

# Operation Specifications
TreeExporter::exportTree
Summary:
Export a tree into a deterministic plain-text outline representation, one line per node.
Algorithm:
1. Traverse the tree in child order.
2. For each node, output a line in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`.
3. Concatenate lines in traversal order.
4. Return the final text.
Related Features:
- Chain/tree textual export
- Deterministic traversal order
Related Classes: TreeNode
Input:
- tree: root TreeNode.
Output:
- A string representation of the tree.
Pre-condition:
- tree is not null.
Post-condition:
- The returned string contains one line per node in traversal order.

TreeExporter::exportToJsonFile
Summary:
Export a tree to a JSON file with deterministic formatting and four-space indentation.
Algorithm:
1. Convert the tree to a JSON string using exportToJson(tree).
2. Write the resulting string to filePath.
3. Overwrite or create the file according to filesystem policy.
Related Features:
- File output
- Deterministic JSON export
Related Classes: TreeNode
Input:
- tree: root TreeNode to export.
- filePath: target filesystem path.
Output:
- None.
Pre-condition:
- tree is not null.
- filePath is writable or creatable.
Post-condition:
- The file at filePath contains a stable pretty-printed JSON representation of tree.

TreeExporter::exportTreeInternal
Summary:
Recursively render a tree node and its descendants into the outline text format used by exportTree.
Algorithm:
1. Render the current node with the current prefix and last-child markers.
2. Recurse into children in stored order.
3. Accumulate the rendered fragments without reordering.
4. Return the full subtree rendering.
Related Features:
- Recursive tree rendering
- Stable child-order traversal
Related Classes: TreeNode
Input:
- node: current TreeNode.
- prefix: indentation/connector prefix accumulated from ancestors.
- isLast: whether the node is the last child among siblings.
- isRoot: whether the node is the tree root.
Output:
- String fragment representing the subtree.
Pre-condition:
- node is not null.
Post-condition:
- The returned string deterministically reflects the subtree structure.

TreeExporter::nodeToDict
Summary:
Convert a tree node into a dictionary/map structure suitable for JSON serialization.
Algorithm:
1. Create a map with keys title, level_seq, level_text, content, and children.
2. Copy the corresponding values from the node.
3. Recursively convert each child using nodeToDict and store the resulting child list in order.
4. Return the map.
Related Features:
- JSON object materialization
- Field-name preservation
- Child-order preservation
Related Classes: TreeNode
Input:
- node: source TreeNode.
Output:
- A map/dictionary representing the node.
Pre-condition:
- node is not null.
Post-condition:
- The returned map contains all required JSON fields and ordered children.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
StrictStrategy::buildTree
Summary:
Build a tree using the strict strategy, which accepts only chains that begin with the root and obey direct parent-child level-sequence relations.
Algorithm:
1. Create a synthetic root TreeNode titled "ROOT" if needed.
2. Initialize a stack or branch with the root.
3. For each chain node:
   a. If it is the first non-root node, ensure it is a direct child of root.
   b. For every next node, verify that its sequence is a child sequence of the current parent.
   c. If valid, create a TreeNode and attach it.
   d. If invalid, reject the chain or stop with an error depending on implementation policy.
4. Return the constructed root tree.
Related Features:
- Strict hierarchy enforcement
- Root-begins-only construction
- Parent-child validation
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy
Input:
- chain: ordered list of ChainNode objects.
Output:
- A TreeNode root of the strict tree.
Pre-condition:
- chain is not null.
Post-condition:
- The output tree contains only structurally valid parent-child links according to strict sequence rules.

StrictStrategy::createTreeNode
Summary:
Create a TreeNode from a ChainNode for strict tree construction.
Algorithm:
1. Allocate a new TreeNode.
2. Copy the semantic fields from the ChainNode.
3. Initialize children and parent references.
4. Return the new node.
Related Features:
- Tree node creation
- Field transfer from parsed chain nodes
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode
Input:
- chainnode: source parsed node.
Output:
- Newly created TreeNode.
Pre-condition:
- chainnode is not null.
Post-condition:
- Returned node is detached and ready for strict attachment.

StrictStrategy::isChild
Summary:
Determine whether childSeq is a direct child sequence of parentSeq.
Algorithm:
1. Check that parentSeq is a prefix of childSeq.
2. Verify that childSeq has exactly one more level element than parentSeq.
3. Return true only if both conditions hold.
Related Features:
- Direct parent-child level relation checking
- Sequence prefix comparison
Related Classes: None
Input:
- parentSeq: candidate parent level sequence.
- childSeq: candidate child level sequence.
Output:
- Boolean indicating direct-child relation.
Pre-condition:
- Both sequences are non-null.
Post-condition:
- No state is modified.

# Operation Specifications
StrictStrategy::buildTree
Summary:
Build a tree using the strict strategy, which accepts only chains that begin with the root and obey direct parent-child level-sequence relations.
Algorithm:
1. Create a synthetic root TreeNode titled "ROOT" if needed.
2. Initialize a stack or branch with the root.
3. For each chain node:
   a. If it is the first non-root node, ensure it is a direct child of root.
   b. For every next node, verify that its sequence is a child sequence of the current parent.
   c. If valid, create a TreeNode and attach it.
   d. If invalid, reject the chain or stop with an error depending on implementation policy.
4. Return the constructed root tree.
Related Features:
- Strict hierarchy enforcement
- Root-begins-only construction
- Parent-child validation
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy
Input:
- chain: ordered list of ChainNode objects.
Output:
- A TreeNode root of the strict tree.
Pre-condition:
- chain is not null.
Post-condition:
- The output tree contains only structurally valid parent-child links according to strict sequence rules.

StrictStrategy::createTreeNode
Summary:
Create a TreeNode from a ChainNode for strict tree construction.
Algorithm:
1. Allocate a new TreeNode.
2. Copy the semantic fields from the ChainNode.
3. Initialize children and parent references.
4. Return the new node.
Related Features:
- Tree node creation
- Field transfer from parsed chain nodes
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode
Input:
- chainnode: source parsed node.
Output:
- Newly created TreeNode.
Pre-condition:
- chainnode is not null.
Post-condition:
- Returned node is detached and ready for strict attachment.

StrictStrategy::isChild
Summary:
Determine whether childSeq is a direct child sequence of parentSeq.
Algorithm:
1. Check that parentSeq is a prefix of childSeq.
2. Verify that childSeq has exactly one more level element than parentSeq.
3. Return true only if both conditions hold.
Related Features:
- Direct parent-child level relation checking
- Sequence prefix comparison
Related Classes: None
Input:
- parentSeq: candidate parent level sequence.
- childSeq: candidate child level sequence.
Output:
- Boolean indicating direct-child relation.
Pre-condition:
- Both sequences are non-null.
Post-condition:
- No state is modified.

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   * Detect whether a line is a valid heading by trying configured level patterns in order, and return the first successful parse as a ChainNode. If no valid pattern matches, treat the line as content rather than a heading.
   * Algorithm:
   * 1. Iterate over patterns in ascending order of priority.
   * 2. For each pattern:
   *    a. Match the line against pattern regex.
   *    b. If matched, convert the matched numbering text into a level sequence.
   *    c. If conversion succeeds and produces a valid level sequence, extract title and content.
   *    d. Return a created ChainNode with the corresponding patternPriority.
   * 3. If no pattern matches or all conversions fail:
   *    a. Return a non-heading ChainNode or an equivalent content node with empty/invalid level information, depending on parser conventions.
   * Related Features:
   * - Pattern-driven heading recognition
   * - First-valid-pattern wins
   * - Number conversion validation
   * - Content fallback for unmatched lines
   * Related Classes: ChainNode, LevelPattern, ParserHelper
   * Input:
   * - line: one line of structured text.
   * Output:
   * - A ChainNode describing the detected heading or content fallback.
   * Pre-condition:
   * - patterns is initialized.
   * - line is not null; empty lines are allowed as content.
   * Post-condition:
   * - The returned node reflects the first valid matching pattern, or a content-like node if no heading is recognized.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public ChainNode detectLevel(final String line)
  {
    if (patterns != null)
    {
      for (LevelPattern pattern : patterns)
      {
        Pattern regex = pattern.getRegex();
        if (regex == null)
        {
          continue;
        }

        Matcher matcher = regex.matcher(line);
        if (!matcher.matches())
        {
          continue;
        }

        String matchedText = matcher.groupCount() >= 1 ? matcher.group(1) : matcher.group();
        EList<Integer> levelSeq = pattern.convertMatchedText(matchedText);
        if (levelSeq != null)
        {
          String title = null;
          String content = "";
          if (matcher.groupCount() >= 2)
          {
            title = matcher.group(2);
            if (matcher.groupCount() >= 3)
            {
              content = matcher.group(3);
            }
          }
          else
          {
            title = line;
          }
          return createChainNode(levelSeq, title, content, matchedText, patterns.indexOf(pattern));
        }
      }
    }

    EList<Integer> levelSeq = new BasicEList<Integer>();
    return createChainNode(levelSeq, line, line, "", -1);
    
  }

  public ChainNode createChainNode(final EList<Integer> levelSeq, final String title, final String content, final String levelText, final int patternPriority)

   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   * Build a document outline tree from a list of chain nodes using the auto-prune strategy. The strategy maintains a branch, defers irregular nodes into a pending queue, merges pending nodes into content when appropriate, and recovers from invalid jumps using sibling-sequence checks. A synthetic root section titled "ROOT" is created even for an empty input.
   * Algorithm:
   * 1. Create a synthetic root TreeNode titled "ROOT" with empty level sequence.
   * 2. Initialize currentBranch with the root and initialize an empty pending queue.
   * 3. For each node in chain:
   *    a. If node is an immediate valid next node:
   *       - Merge any pending nodes that appear before it into the current node content in arrival order.
   *       - Attach the node at the nearest suitable ancestor.
   *       - Update currentBranch to the new valid branch.
   *    b. Otherwise:
   *       - Push node into the pending queue.
   *       - If pending size reaches 3:
   *         i. Check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence.
   *         ii. If yes, attach them to the tree in order.
   *         iii. If no, merge the oldest pending node into current node content.
   * 4. After all nodes are processed, merge any remaining pending nodes into the current node content in arrival order.
   * 5. Return the root tree.
   * Related Features:
   * - Synthetic root creation
   * - Auto-prune pending queue handling
   * - Immediate sibling-sequence recovery
   * - Content merging in traversal order
   * - Branch update after attachment
   * Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode
   * Input:
   * - chain: ordered list of ChainNode objects parsed from text.
   * Output:
   * - A TreeNode representing the root of the constructed outline tree.
   * Pre-condition:
   * - chain may be empty, but must be iterable.
   * - Each ChainNode should have a parsed levelSeq or be representable as content-only input.
   * Post-condition:
   * - The result is a tree rooted at a synthetic node titled "ROOT".
   * - All input nodes are either attached into the tree or merged into content according to auto-prune rules.

   * @generated NOT
   */

    root.setLevelSeq(new BasicEList<Integer>());
    root.setLevelText("");
    root.setContent("");
    root.getChildren().clear();
    root.setParent(null);

    EList<TreeNode> currentBranch = new BasicEList<TreeNode>();

    for (ChainNode node : chain)

        }

            }

          else

            currentNodeRef[0].concatNode(pending.removeFirst());
          }
        }
      }
    }

                case ROMAN -> {
                    Integer value = Utils.romanToInt(text);
                    yield value != null ? value : 0;
                }
                case CHINESE -> {
                    Long value = Utils.chineseToInt(text);
                    yield value != null ? value.intValue() : 0;
                }
                case LETTER -> (int) text.charAt(0) - (int) 'A' + 1;
                case CIRCLED -> (int) text.charAt(0) - (int) '\u2460' + 1;
            };
  }

   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   * Build a document outline tree from a list of chain nodes using the auto-prune strategy. The strategy maintains a branch, defers irregular nodes into a pending queue, merges pending nodes into content when appropriate, and recovers from invalid jumps using sibling-sequence checks. A synthetic root section titled "ROOT" is created even for an empty input.
   * Algorithm:
   * 1. Create a synthetic root TreeNode titled "ROOT" with empty level sequence.
   * 2. Initialize currentBranch with the root and initialize an empty pending queue.
   * 3. For each node in chain:
   *    a. If node is an immediate valid next node:
   *       - Merge any pending nodes that appear before it into the current node content in arrival order.
   *       - Attach the node at the nearest suitable ancestor.
   *       - Update currentBranch to the new valid branch.
   *    b. Otherwise:
   *       - Push node into the pending queue.
   *       - If pending size reaches 3:
   *         i. Check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence.
   *         ii. If yes, attach them to the tree in order.
   *         iii. If no, merge the oldest pending node into current node content.
   * 4. After all nodes are processed, merge any remaining pending nodes into the current node content in arrival order.
   * 5. Return the root tree.
   * Related Features:
   * - Synthetic root creation
   * - Auto-prune pending queue handling
   * - Immediate sibling-sequence recovery
   * - Content merging in traversal order
   * - Branch update after attachment
   * Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode
   * Input:
   * - chain: ordered list of ChainNode objects parsed from text.
   * Output:
   * - A TreeNode representing the root of the constructed outline tree.
   * Pre-condition:
   * - chain may be empty, but must be iterable.
   * - Each ChainNode should have a parsed levelSeq or be representable as content-only input.
   * Post-condition:
   * - The result is a tree rooted at a synthetic node titled "ROOT".
   * - All input nodes are either attached into the tree or merged into content according to auto-prune rules.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->

   *        annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */

  {
    TreeNode root = ArborparserFactory.eINSTANCE.createTreeNode();
    root.setTitle("ROOT");
    root.setLevelSeq(new BasicEList<Integer>());
    root.setLevelText("");
    root.setContent("");
    root.getChildren().clear();
    root.setParent(null);

    EList<TreeNode> currentBranch = new BasicEList<TreeNode>();

    for (ChainNode node : chain)
    {
      if (isImmNext(currentNodeRef[0].getLevelSeq(), node.getLevelSeq()))

        while (!pending.isEmpty())
        {
          currentNodeRef[0].concatNode(pending.removeFirst());
        }
        addNodeToTree(node, currentBranch, currentNodeRef);

        if (pending.size() >= 3)

          {
            while (!pending.isEmpty())
            {
              addNodeToTree(pending.removeFirst(), currentBranch, currentNodeRef);
            }
          }
          else
          {
            currentNodeRef[0].concatNode(pending.removeFirst());
          }
        }
      }
    }

    while (!pending.isEmpty())
    {

    }

    return root;

The strategy maintains a branch, defers irregular nodes into a pending queue, merges pending nodes into content when appropriate, and recovers from invalid jumps using sibling-sequence checks. A synthetic root section titled "ROOT" is created even for an empty input.
   * Algorithm:
   * 1. Create a synthetic root TreeNode titled "ROOT" with empty level sequence.
   * 2. Initialize currentBranch with the root and initialize an empty pending queue.
   * 3. For each node in chain:
   *    a. If node is an immediate valid next node:
   *       - Merge any pending nodes that appear before it into the current node content in arrival order.
   *       - Attach the node at the nearest suitable ancestor.
   *       - Update currentBranch to the new valid branch.
   *    b. Otherwise:
   *       - Push node into the pending queue.
   *       - If pending size reaches 3:
   *         i. Check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence.
   *         ii. If yes, attach them to the tree in order.
   *         iii. If no, merge the oldest pending node into current node content.
   * 4. After all nodes are processed, merge any remaining pending nodes into the current node content in arrival order.
   * 5. Return the root tree.
   * Related Features:
   * - Synthetic root creation
   * - Auto-prune pending queue handling
   * - Immediate sibling-sequence recovery
   * - Content merging in traversal order
   * - Branch update after attachment
   * Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode
   * Input:
   * - chain: ordered list of ChainNode objects parsed from text.
   * Output:
   * - A TreeNode representing the root of the constructed outline tree.
   * Pre-condition:
   * - chain may be empty, but must be iterable.
   * - Each ChainNode should have a parsed levelSeq or be representable as content-only input.
   * Post-condition:
   * - The result is a tree rooted at a synthetic node titled "ROOT".
   * - All input nodes are either attached into the tree or merged into content according to auto-prune rules.

    root.setTitle("ROOT");
    root.setLevelSeq(new BasicEList<Integer>());
    root.setLevelText("");
    root.setContent("");
    root.getChildren().clear();
    root.setParent(null);

    EList<TreeNode> currentBranch = new BasicEList<TreeNode>();

    TreeNode[] currentNodeRef = new TreeNode[] { root };
    Deque<ChainNode> pending = new java.util.ArrayDeque<ChainNode>();

    for (ChainNode node : chain)
    {
      if (isImmNext(currentNodeRef[0].getLevelSeq(), node.getLevelSeq()))
      {
        while (!pending.isEmpty())
        {
          currentNodeRef[0].concatNode(pending.removeFirst());
        }
        addNodeToTree(node, currentBranch, currentNodeRef);
      }
      else
      {
        pending.addLast(node);
        if (pending.size() >= 3)
        {
          if (isAllNotImmNodesSiblings(pending))
          {
            while (!pending.isEmpty())
            {
              addNodeToTree(pending.removeFirst(), currentBranch, currentNodeRef);
            }
          }
          else
          {
            currentNodeRef[0].concatNode(pending.removeFirst());
          }
        }
      }
    }

    while (!pending.isEmpty())
    {
      currentNodeRef[0].concatNode(pending.removeFirst());
    }

    return root;
  }

   * Summary:
   * Build a document outline tree from a list of chain nodes using the auto-prune strategy. The strategy maintains a branch, defers irregular nodes into a pending queue, merges pending nodes into content when appropriate, and recovers from invalid jumps using sibling-sequence checks. A synthetic root section titled "ROOT" is created even for an empty input.
   * Algorithm:
   * 1. Create a synthetic root TreeNode titled "ROOT" with empty level sequence.
   * 2. Initialize currentBranch with the root and initialize an empty pending queue.
   * 3. For each node in chain:
   *    a. If node is an immediate valid next node:
   *       - Merge any pending nodes that appear before it into the current node content in arrival order.
   *       - Attach the node at the nearest suitable ancestor.
   *       - Update currentBranch to the new valid branch.
   *    b. Otherwise:
   *       - Push node into the pending queue.
   *       - If pending size reaches 3:
   *         i. Check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence.
   *         ii. If yes, attach them to the tree in order.
   *         iii. If no, merge the oldest pending node into current node content.
   * 4. After all nodes are processed, merge any remaining pending nodes into the current node content in arrival order.
   * 5. Return the root tree.
   * Related Features:
   * - Synthetic root creation
   * - Auto-prune pending queue handling
   * - Immediate sibling-sequence recovery
   * - Content merging in traversal order
   * - Branch update after attachment
   * Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode
   * Input:
   * - chain: ordered list of ChainNode objects parsed from text.
   * Output:
   * - A TreeNode representing the root of the constructed outline tree.
   * Pre-condition:
   * - chain may be empty, but must be iterable.
   * - Each ChainNode should have a parsed levelSeq or be representable as content-only input.
   * Post-condition:

    currentBranch.add(root);

    for (ChainNode node : chain)
    {

      {
        while (!pending.isEmpty())
        {
          currentNodeRef[0].concatNode(pending.removeFirst());
        }
        addNodeToTree(node, currentBranch, currentNodeRef);
      }

        if (pending.size() >= 3)

          }
        }
      }
    }

    while (!pending.isEmpty())

    }

   *         iii. If no, merge the oldest pending node into current node content.

          }

   * Summary:
   * Build a document outline tree from a list of chain nodes using the auto-prune strategy. The strategy maintains a branch, defers irregular nodes into a pending queue, merges pending nodes into content when appropriate, and recovers from invalid jumps using sibling-sequence checks. A synthetic root section titled "ROOT" is created even for an empty input.
   * Algorithm:
   * 1. Create a synthetic root TreeNode titled "ROOT" with empty level sequence.
   * 2. Initialize currentBranch with the root and initialize an empty pending queue.
   * 3. For each node in chain:
   *    a. If node is an immediate valid next node:
   *       - Merge any pending nodes that appear before it into the current node content in arrival order.
   *       - Attach the node at the nearest suitable ancestor.
   *       - Update currentBranch to the new valid branch.
   *    b. Otherwise:
   *       - Push node into the pending queue.
   *       - If pending size reaches 3:
   *         i. Check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence.
   *         ii. If yes, attach them to the tree in order.
   *         iii. If no, merge the oldest pending node into current node content.
   * 4. After all nodes are processed, merge any remaining pending nodes into the current node content in arrival order.
   * 5. Return the root tree.
   * Related Features:
   * - Synthetic root creation
   * - Auto-prune pending queue handling
   * - Immediate sibling-sequence recovery
   * - Content merging in traversal order
   * - Branch update after attachment
   * Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode
   * Input:
   * - chain: ordered list of ChainNode objects parsed from text.
   * Output:
   * - A TreeNode representing the root of the constructed outline tree.
   * Pre-condition:
   * - chain may be empty, but must be iterable.
   * - Each ChainNode should have a parsed levelSeq or be representable as content-only input.
   * Post-condition:
   * - The result is a tree rooted at a synthetic node titled "ROOT".
   * - All input nodes are either attached into the tree or merged into content according to auto-prune rules.

          }
        }
      }
    }

3. Related Features: a list of structural or behavior features within this class that shall be accessed;
4. Related Classes: a list of classes and data types defined in **Class Diagram** that shall be accessed, in the format of `Related Classes: ClsA, CLsB, ...` or `Related Classes: None`;
5. Input: the input parameters, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
7. Pre-condition: the condition that the system and the input must satisfy before the operation is executed;
8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

Finish this task by following the guidelines below.
1. Take the principle of modularization into account.
2. For each operation, determine its functional boundary based on the given requirement. Ensure high cohesion and low coupling.
3. If there is any unspecified details, such as undefined constants, rates, and ratios, then you must infer them.
4. Make sure that all requirements can be covered.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

class AutoPruneStrategy {
    addNodeAndUpdateBranch(node : ChainNode, currentBranch : List<TreeNode>) : void
    addNodeToTree(node : ChainNode, currentBranch : List<TreeNode>, currentNodeRef : node) : void
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    createTreeNode(chainnode : ChainNode) : TreeNode
    isAllNotImmNodesSiblings(queue : Deque) : void
}
class BaseNode {
    content : String
    levelSeq : List<int>
    levelText : String
    title : String
    concatNode(node : BaseNode) : void
}
class ChainNode {
    patternPriority : int
}
class ChainParser {
    patterns : List<LevelPattern>
    createChainNode(levelSeq : List<int>, title : String, content : String, levelText : String, patternPriority : int) : ChainNode
    detectLevel(line : String) : ChainNode
    parseToChain(text : String) : List<ChainNode>
}

    description : String
    failOnConvert : boolean
    fixedLevelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>
    maxLevel : int
    minLevel : int
    numberType : NumberType
    regexText : String
    separator : String
    helper : ParserHelper

    getRegex() : Pattern
}

    getNumberPattern(numberType : NumberType) : String
}

    maxLevel : int
    minLevel : int
    numberType : NumberType
    prefixRegex : String
    separator : String
    suffixRegex : String
    build() : LevelPattern
    copySelf() : PatternBuilder
    modify(newPrefixRegex : String, newMinLevel : int) : PatternBuilder
    validate() : void
}
class StrictStrategy {
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    createTreeNode(chainnode : ChainNode) : TreeNode
    isChild(parentSeq : List<EIntegerObject>, childSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : boolean
}
class TreeBuilder {
    strategy : TreeBuildingStrategy
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
}
abstract class TreeBuildingStrategy {
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    getLastLevel(levelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : int
    getPrefix(levelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : List<EIntegerObject>
    isImmNext(frontSeq : List<EIntegerObject>, backSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : boolean
    isRoot(node : BaseNode) : boolean
}
class TreeExporter {
    escapeJson(s : String) : String
    exportChain(chain : List<ChainNode>) : String
    exportToJson(tree : TreeNode) : String
    exportToJsonFile(tree : TreeNode, filePath : Path) : void
    exportTree(tree : TreeNode) : String
    exportTreeInternal(node : TreeNode, prefix : String, isLast : boolean, isRoot : boolean) : String
    nodeToDict(node : TreeNode) : EMap
    toJson(obj : EJavaObject, indent : int) : String
}
class TreeNode {
    children : List<TreeNode>
    parent : TreeNode
    addChild(child : TreeNode) : void
    getFullContent() : String
    mergeAllChildren() : void
}
enum NumberType {
    ARABIC
    ROMAN
    CHINESE
    LETTER
    CIRCLED
}

TreeNode --|> BaseNode

TreeNode --> TreeNode : parent  'opposite: children

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
TreeNode::mergeAllChildren
Summary:
Merge all descendants’ content into this node’s content and clear or collapse child structure according to subtree-merging behavior.
Algorithm:
1. Traverse all children in order.
2. For each child, obtain its full content.
3. Append descendant content to this node’s content without extra separators.
4. Recurse as needed so that descendant content is fully consumed.
5. If required by the implementation, detach or keep children while ensuring merged content is retained.
Related Features:
- Descendant content collection
- Subtree content collapsing
Related Classes: TreeNode
Input:
- None.
Output:
- void. The current node’s content and possibly its subtree state are updated.
Pre-condition:
- The subtree is acyclic and structurally valid.
Post-condition:
- This node’s content includes the content of all descendants in traversal order.
- Tree links remain consistent for any retained structure.

TreeNode::addChild
Summary:
Attach a child tree node to this node and establish the reverse parent link consistently.
Algorithm:
1. Validate child is non-null.
2. Append child to this.children in order.
3. Set child.parent to this node.
4. If the child previously had another parent, that prior relationship is considered replaced by the new attachment.
Related Features:
- Parent-child link maintenance
- Ordered child insertion
Related Classes: TreeNode
Input:
- child: node to be added as a child.
Output:
- void. The tree structure is updated in place.
Pre-condition:
- child is non-null.
- The caller ensures the attachment is structurally valid.
Post-condition:
- child appears in this.children.
- child.parent references this node.

TreeNode::getFullContent
Summary:
Return the complete textual content of this node by combining the node’s own content with the content collected from descendants in traversal order.
Algorithm:
1. Start with this node’s content.
2. Recursively traverse children in stored order.
3. Append each descendant’s full content directly, without extra separators.
4. Return the accumulated string.
Related Features:
- Content aggregation from descendants
- Traversal-order concatenation
Related Classes: TreeNode
Input:
- None.
Output:
- String representing the full merged content of the subtree.
Pre-condition:
- The tree must not contain cycles.
Post-condition:
- The return value reflects content collected in deterministic traversal order.

Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

# Operation Specifications
AutoPruneStrategy::addNodeToTree
Summary:
Attach one chain node into the current tree using the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is a prefix of the node’s sequence, and merge any earlier pending nodes when appropriate.
Algorithm:
1. Determine the nearest ancestor in currentBranch whose level sequence is a prefix of node.levelSeq.
2. Create a TreeNode from the ChainNode if needed.
3. Attach the new tree node as a child of that ancestor.
4. If there are pending nodes that appear before the current node, merge them into currentNodeRef’s content in arrival order.
5. If the pending queue has three nodes, evaluate whether they form an immediate sibling sequence:
   - If yes, attach them in order.
   - Otherwise, merge the oldest pending node into currentNodeRef’s content and remove it from the queue.
6. Update the current node reference and branch metadata accordingly.
Related Features:
- Nearest-prefix ancestor search
- Tree attachment for auto-prune strategy
- Pending queue merge/flush policy
- Sibling-sequence validation
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy
Input:
- node: the ChainNode to attach.
- currentBranch: ordered TreeNode list representing the latest valid path.
- currentNodeRef: reference to the current attached node used for content merging.
Output:
- void. Tree structure, branch state, and pending queue are updated.
Pre-condition:
- currentBranch contains a root and represents a valid attached path.
- node is non-null.
- currentNodeRef refers to the latest node in the current branch or a valid current attachment target.
Post-condition:
- node is attached to exactly one suitable parent when resolvable.
- Deferred nodes are merged or attached according to the pending policy.
- Tree parent-child consistency is preserved.

AutoPruneStrategy::addNodeAndUpdateBranch
Summary:
Update the current valid branch while processing one chain node. If the node is an immediate valid next node of the current branch, attach it to the nearest suitable ancestor and refresh the branch. Otherwise, defer the node by placing it into the pending queue.
Algorithm:
1. Inspect the incoming ChainNode against the current branch and the latest attached node.
2. If the node satisfies the immediate-next relation, call addNodeToTree to attach it.
3. After attachment, rebuild currentBranch so it represents the latest valid path from ROOT to the newly attached node.
4. If the node is not immediate-next, append it to the pending queue.
5. If pending nodes accumulate to a resolvable state, let addNodeToTree / sibling-check logic decide whether to attach or merge them.
Related Features:
- Current branch maintenance for auto-prune tree building
- Pending queue handling for irregular chains
- Immediate-next relation checking through TreeBuildingStrategy
- Tree attachment and branch refresh
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy
Input:
- node: the ChainNode to be processed.
- currentBranch: ordered TreeNode list from root to current attachment point; may be updated in place.
Output:
- void. The tree structure, pending queue state, and currentBranch are updated as a side effect.
Pre-condition:
- currentBranch is initialized and contains at least the synthetic root.
- node is non-null and has a parsed level sequence.
- The strategy’s internal tree root and pending queue are initialized.
Post-condition:
- If node is immediate-next, it is attached to the tree and currentBranch points to the latest valid branch.
- If node is not immediate-next, it is stored for later resolution.
- Parent-child links remain consistent after any attachment.

AutoPruneStrategy::createTreeNode
Summary:
Create a TreeNode instance from a ChainNode by copying its base semantic fields into a tree node representation.
Algorithm:
1. Allocate a new TreeNode.
2. Copy title, levelSeq, levelText, and content from the ChainNode/BaseNode fields.
3. Initialize children to an empty list and parent to null.
4. Return the created TreeNode.
Related Features:
- Node conversion from chain representation to tree representation
- Tree node initialization
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, BaseNode
Input:
- chainnode: source chain node to convert.
Output:
- TreeNode: a new tree node with copied structural and text fields.
Pre-condition:
- chainnode is non-null.
Post-condition:
- Returned TreeNode is detached from any parent and has no children initially.
- Semantic fields match the source node.

AutoPruneStrategy::buildTree
Summary:
Build a document outline tree using the auto-prune strategy, which tolerates irregular level jumps by buffering unresolved nodes and recovering to the nearest suitable ancestor.
Algorithm:
1. Create a synthetic ROOT TreeNode with empty level sequence.
2. Initialize currentBranch with ROOT and initialize an empty pending queue.
3. Iterate through the ChainNode list in order.
4. For each node:
   - If it is immediate-next, attach it using addNodeAndUpdateBranch.
   - Otherwise, store it in the pending queue.
5. When pending nodes become resolvable, merge or attach them according to the three-node queue policy.
6. After all nodes are processed, merge all remaining pending nodes into the current node’s content.
7. Return ROOT.
Related Features:
- Synthetic root creation
- Auto-prune recovery logic
- Pending queue flush at end of input
- Ordered document reconstruction
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode
Input:
- chain: ordered list of parsed chain nodes.
Output:
- TreeNode: the synthetic ROOT of the constructed tree.
Pre-condition:
- chain may be empty but must be a valid list object.
- The strategy has access to a valid internal tree-building context.
Post-condition:
- A tree is returned even for empty input.
- The tree root is titled "ROOT" by convention.
- All nodes are either attached or merged into content according to auto-prune rules.

AutoPruneStrategy::isAllNotImmNodesSiblings
Summary:
Determine whether all nodes currently in the pending queue form an immediate sibling sequence, enabling batch attachment instead of content merging.
Algorithm:
1. If the queue has fewer than 3 nodes, return false unless the implementation can verify sibling adjacency from the available nodes.
2. Compare every adjacent pair in the queue using the immediate sibling relation derived from level sequences.
3. Return true only if all nodes are mutually consistent as siblings in order.
4. Otherwise return false.
Related Features:
- Pending queue analysis
- Immediate sibling sequence detection
Related Classes: TreeBuildingStrategy
Input:
- queue: deque of pending nodes.
Output:
- boolean-like result indicating whether all queued non-immediate nodes are siblings in order.
Pre-condition:
- queue is non-null and contains ChainNode objects or equivalent pending-node entries.
Post-condition:
- No structural mutation is required; the method is a predicate.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.

1. Create a synthetic ROOT TreeNode.

- Invalid non-root-start chains are rejected.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.

# Operation Specifications
PatternBuilder::modify
Summary:
Derive a new builder configuration by changing the prefix regex and minimum level while keeping other settings unchanged.
Algorithm:
1. Clone the current builder by calling copySelf.
2. Replace prefixRegex with newPrefixRegex.
3. Replace minLevel with newMinLevel.
4. Return the modified builder.
Related Features:
- Builder derivation
- Selective configuration update
Related Classes: None
Input:
- newPrefixRegex: replacement prefix regular expression.
- newMinLevel: new minimum supported level, typically a non-negative integer.
Output:
- PatternBuilder: a new builder instance reflecting the requested modification.
Pre-condition:
- newMinLevel must not exceed maxLevel.
- newPrefixRegex must be syntactically usable in the final regex composition.
Post-condition:
- The original builder remains unchanged.
- The returned builder contains the updated fields.

PatternBuilder::copySelf
Summary:
Create a copy of the current builder so modifications can be applied independently without affecting the original builder.
Algorithm:
1. Allocate a new PatternBuilder.
2. Copy maxLevel, minLevel, numberType, prefixRegex, separator, and suffixRegex.
3. Return the cloned builder.
Related Features:
- Builder cloning for pattern derivation
Related Classes: None
Input:
- None.
Output:
- PatternBuilder: a shallow value copy of the current builder configuration.
Pre-condition:
- The builder instance is initialized.
Post-condition:
- The returned builder can be modified independently.

PatternBuilder::validate
Summary:
Validate that the builder configuration is internally consistent and sufficient to build a usable LevelPattern.
Algorithm:
1. Check that minLevel and maxLevel define a valid inclusive range.
2. Check that numberType or fixed-level configuration is present as required.
3. Check that regex fragments and separator values are non-null and compatible.
4. Throw or signal an error if any constraint is violated.
Related Features:
- Builder configuration validation
- Pattern construction safety
Related Classes: NumberType
Input:
- None.
Output:
- void. Validation succeeds silently or raises an error on invalid configuration.
Pre-condition:
- Builder fields must already be assigned.
Post-condition:
- A valid builder can be used to create LevelPattern; invalid state is rejected.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```
